source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #381 (branch fix/193-register-mapping at head eab5e2fac87cf9e778b34144ebe863d87335f48f — the #193 change (the masm trait’s explicit per-target register mapping, phys_loc(vreg) -> PhysLoc { Reg | Slot }, homing the x86_64 and riscv64 virtual registers in physical registers instead of emulating the A64 register file in frame slots) merged with current main 2d653bfae0bd3ac995c17a0d26154f531762d28c (PR #379, PR #382 and PR #383), plus a size-gate re-baseline, plus a follow-up fix forcing a REX prefix when sign-extending a byte source homed in RSI/RDI (Codex P2 on the PR) and a second size-gate re-baseline for that fix; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45817815567, 45817829767 and 45817843974 against the branch produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Second re-baseline for PR #381 (#193, per-target physical register mapping for the x86_64 and riscv64 baseline-JIT encoders), following the Codex P2 fix that forces the bare REX prefix in movsx_vreg32 when the byte form’s source register sits in r/m fields 4..=7 without REX.B — since #193, vregs 9/10 home in RSI/RDI, whose byte forms SIL/DIL a REX-less encoding misreads as DH/BH (commit 876525d6c171178e6b4b312e7252dcde88c43978, on top of the first re-baseline at 099876d). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45817858119, 45817871880 and 45817883664 on main at 2d653bfae0bd3ac995c17a0d26154f531762d28c (PR #383); all three runs pass the gate; the main control is byte-identical to the previous campaign’s main control on every series — PR #383 touched only a CI workflow file — and thereby byte-identical to the checked-in baseline on the twelve series of the baseline, core and core-nosimd configurations, below it on the core-aot series (104 B / 16 B in release and 160 B / 64 B in release-size) and on the core-jit series (12,864 B / 9,408 B in release and 5,704 B / 3,536 B in release-size — the #193 delta net of PR #382’s shrink already on main), and below the retained baselines on the twelve series of the three configurations that link telomere-component). This PR’s own delta against the main control remains confined to the core-jit configuration: in release, stripped file +12,912 B and stripped .text +9,456 B; in release-size, stripped file +5,736 B and stripped .text +3,568 B — the #193 register-mapping encodings plus the REX-forcing branch in the x86_64 encoder’s movsx path, which only the core-jit configuration links with the jit feature. Every other series is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Against the checked-in baseline only the four core-jit series grow (+48 B / +48 B in release and +32 B / +32 B in release-size — the Codex P2 fix alone, the #193 delta having been re-baselined at 099876d), so only those four series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and every other baseline is retained, following the established practice of re-baselining growth only. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples; the pull-request run 45817805255 at the same head measured byte-identically to the branch samples on every series. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +11.42% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,648 B), unchanged because that series’ baseline is retained; the re-baselined core-jit series stand at +8.32% (release stripped file, 1,989,584 B to 2,155,128 B), +7.48% (release stripped .text), +4.57% (release-size stripped file) and +4.24% (release-size stripped .text). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
